subject: KPI bridging playbook & QBR check-in — latency / cost / uptime / usage
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: KPI bridging playbook & QBR check-in — latency / cost / uptime / usage

Team — attaching the July dashboard and a short playbook draft for bridging the gaps I flagged in last week’s ops readout (attachment: kpi_dashboard_july_v2.pdf). Narrow summary: latency P95 on hosted API is up 18% month-over-month during peak evening hours, unit cost per 1k tokens increased ~12% due to longer average seq lengths for a handful of tenants, and two short uptime blips (region-eu) were traced to a scheduled network maintenance that didn’t propagate fallback policy correctly.

I outlined immediate containment + medium-term remediation owners in the playbook (last section):
- Latency P95 investigation: owner = Jonas (deep-dive + hypothesis list by Tue)
- Cost regression: owner = Markus (work with Pricing to validate token-logging and batching impact)
- Uptime blips: owner = Irene (rollback of fallback rules + postmortem docs)
- QBR material for Acme: owner = Naomi (consolidate notes + send to Mira by Thu)

Request: please review the dashboard and the playbook sections I flagged and reply with one-line commit or an alternate owner by EOD Mon. I’ll collate asks into a 30-min leadership sync (Weds) to finalize the QBR artifact and confirm canary timings.

Quick asks in the doc:
- Jonas: include top-3 contributing models and sequence-length distribution for the P95 window
- Markus: run the batching-sensitivity runbook and attach a short table of expected cost delta for 3 quant/bs combinations
- Irene: confirm the fallback policy settings we want to re-enable and whether the network maintenance SOP needs a change for cross-region propagation

Attachments: kpi_dashboard_july_v2.pdf (pdf), qbr-ask-summary.docx (docx)

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Platform Metrics & Insights
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KPI bridging playbook & QBR check-in — latency / cost / uptime / usage

Naomi — got it. I’ll take ownership of the latency P95 deep-dive. Immediate notes:
- I see correlation with increased long-tail prompt patterns between 18:00-22:00 PT (also corroborated by KV-cache miss rate rising).
- Hypotheses I’ll test: longer historical context, increased system messages, and less effective batching for those tenant mixes.

Action plan (will deliver by Tue EOD):
1) Query: top 5 tenants contributing to 95th percentile during the window (presenting per-model breakdown)
2) KV-cache hit/miss trend + heatmap for the same window
3) Proposed mitigations: lighter context truncation policy (A/B), aggressive prefix caching for eligible tenants, and temporary burst capacity during evening peaks to avoid latency SLO violations.

I’ll attach a short results spreadsheet once the initial queries finish.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Inference Ops
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KPI bridging playbook & QBR check-in — latency / cost / uptime / usage

Looping in my quick read. I ran a micro-batching sensitivity pass and exported an evidence sheet (attachment: batching-analysis.xlsx). Early signals: batching improvements can recoup ~6–8% cost at current traffic profiles but yield modest P95 improvements unless combined with KV-hit optimizations. Two asks for the next 72 hours:
- Ops: Jonas, can you prioritize KV-cache hypothesis validation so we know whether to bias toward batching vs cache-first?
- Platform: Irene, we should hold a short change window for the fallback rule rollback; prefer 01:00–03:00 PT to minimize impact.

Also: for the QBR slide deck (Acme + internal exec readout) I propose we include a one-slide tradeoff matrix (cost vs latency vs risk) and a timeline showing canary -> roll -> monitor. Happy to draft the slide if Naomi passes the final numbers to me.

Attachment: batching-analysis.xlsx (xlsx).

— Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Platform Reliability
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KPI bridging playbook & QBR check-in — latency / cost / uptime / usage

Thanks — quick status update from infra: I confirmed the fallback-policy regression was a rollout gap in the orchestration config for eu-region maintenance. I pushed an emergency patch to re-enable cross-region fallback propagation and will publish the postmortem draft by Mon. For the change window Markus proposed (01:00–03:00 PT) I prefer 01:30 start to give runbooks a buffer.

I also validated that the network maintenance SOP needs a one-paragraph addition to call out the orchestration propagation step — I’ll add that to Confluence and link it in the postmortem.

Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Platform Engineering
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Mira Patel <mira.patel@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Acme Analytics SRE <sre@acme-analytics.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 14:06:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: KPI bridging playbook & QBR check-in — latency / cost / uptime / usage

Mira — forwarding our internal playbook draft and the July dashboard ahead of our QBR prep. Short summary for Acme: we observed higher P95 latency during your peak usage window tied to longer average request context; our proposed plan (we’ll review in the QBR) is:
1) Short-term: temporary burst capacity to stabilize P95 for the next 2 weeks (Jonas to own run)
2) Medium-term: selective batching + prefix caching rollouts for tenant cohorts who tolerate minimal pre/post-processing (Markus to own cost/econ modeling)
3) Post-QBR: automated monitoring alert for sequence-length shifts and a rollbackable canary for any batching changes.

Attached: kpi_dashboard_july_v2.pdf, qbr-ask-summary.docx

Can you confirm whether Thur 05 Aug at 10:00 PT works for a joint prep sync? If that slot doesn’t work, send a preferred time and we’ll adjust.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Platform Metrics & Insights
Redwood Inference
